name: XNU source (12.1)
summary: Apple's open-source XNU 4903.221.2, the kernel family used by iOS 12.1.
detail: Tag xnu-4903.221.2, distributed under APSL-2.0. This is source, not a bootable kernel. The n66 block-device driver needs headers and symbols from the XNU version that matches your kernelcache.

name: n66 QEMU source
summary: Aleph Research's QEMU fork with the iPhone6splus-n66-s8000 machine.
detail: GPL-2.0, pinned commit 2694993f. The host build in host/build-qemu.sh downloads this same archive. Upstream QEMU does not have the machine model. The fork patches the guest kernel in memory; read docs/LEGAL.md.

name: Kernelcache (decoded)
summary: kernelcache.release.n66.out, the decoded Mach-O kernel from your iOS 12.1 IPSW.
detail: The machine loads a decoded Mach-O directly; it does not use iBoot. Decode kernelcache.release.n66 with host/prepare-artifacts.py on a computer. The kernel must be iOS 12.1 build 16B92 because the n66 machine's patch addresses are hard-coded for it.

name: Device tree (decoded)
detail: XNU's ARM64 entry point parses Apple's Device Tree, not a standard FDT. The decoded blob describes the n66 memory map, interrupts, timers and UART used by the machine model.

name: Block-device driver
summary: aleph_bdev_drv.bin, compiled against your kernel's symbols.
detail: Position-independent kernel code that exposes the two HFS+ images as disk0 and disk1. Build it from xnu-qemu-arm64-tools with a matching XNU source tree and the decoded kernel's symbols; see host/README.md.
license: Upstream project — no explicit license file; user built

name: Main disk
summary: hfs.main, a prepared HFS+ image containing the iOS system volume.
detail: The upstream macOS procedure copies the iOS 12.1 system volume into a resized ramdisk, edits fstab and launch daemons, and patches launchd. This is Apple code and must stay local. It is not derivable from an IPSW by this app.

source.hint: hfs.main prepared with the upstream hdiutil procedure; see host/DISKS.md

name: Secondary disk
summary: hfs.sec, the prepared HFS+ image mounted at /private/var.
detail: A second disk image built from the same update DMG. The machine exposes it as disk1; the guest fstab mounts it read-write. Losing it or killing QEMU uncleanly can require repairing the HFS+ volume.

source.hint: hfs.sec prepared with the upstream hdiutil procedure; see host/DISKS.md

name: Ramdisk (decoded)
summary: 048-32651-104.dmg.out, optional for the custom-disk boot path.
detail: The decoded restore ramdisk. The n66 command used by this project boots from hfs.main instead, so this is not required. It is useful if you are experimenting with a ramdisk-root boot.
